# Rising Tide. One complete, authored scene for each of the 125 campaign events.
# @ CLASS## BACKGROUND METHOD; > BACKGROUND METHOD CAMERA_X changes a shot.
# Dialogue is ASCII for the cartridge font. Narration is an explicit story montage,
# not evidence that a player has raced in this story-only build.

@ D01 GARAGE FACE
NIA: Mind the jack. It rolls toward anything expensive.
YOU: Is that why you parked my car beside it?
NIA: Your car? These are the garage keys. The car keys are the small, disappointing ones.
YOU: You said there was work.
NIA: There is. Sunline needs another pair of hands, and tonight the club needs another driver.
> MEET PAN 80
MINA: First night, first photograph. Try to look as if you meant to come here.
YOU: What do I owe you?
NIA: Bring the car home straight. We can work out the rest over breakfast.

@ D02 MEET PAN
JULES: That's Nia's loaner. Does she know you've taken it outside?
YOU: She gave me the keys.
JULES: She gave me a spanner once. Different expression on her face, though.
MINA: Jules delivers everything except a straight answer. You're in the next club heat together.
JULES: Start beside me. Finish wherever your dignity permits.

@ D03 GARAGE FACE
NIA: Mrs. Vale paid for her repair in oranges. Again.
YOU: Can oranges pay the rent?
NIA: Not yet. Tonight's corner-store meet can cover the electricity, though.
CALDER: Store closes at nine. Barriers go up after. Nobody moves until my marshal gives the all-clear.
YOU: You're Calder?
CALDER: Depends who's asking. If you scratch that loaner, I'm the one Nia phones.

@ D04 GARAGE FACE
YOU: This envelope was under the till.
NIA: Leave it. It's the lease renewal.
YOU: Another rent rise?
NIA: Another month to decide whether this place is worth keeping. I'd rather spend it working than worrying.
YOU: Put me down for tonight's heat, then.
NIA: Good. And put that envelope somewhere I don't have to look at it while I eat.

@ D05 MARINA RADIO
MINA: The last heat is short. Everyone else has gone home for dinner.
YOU: You stayed.
MINA: Someone has to take a photograph that isn't Jules pointing at himself.
NIA: One clean run, then home. I saved you a plate.
YOU: You cook here too?
NIA: I heat things here. Manage your expectations.

@ D06 MEET PAN
KADE: You kept a tidy line in that last heat. Want to try the longer loop before they take the barriers down?
JULES: That jacket's from the Foundry clubs. Careful. They consider braking a personal insult.
YOU: One exhibition. Nothing on the line.
KADE: Fine by me. A clean start and a handshake at the end.
> FOUNDRY PAN 210
NARRATOR: EXHIBITION. By the second corner, Kade's taillights are two bends ahead.
YOU: I couldn't even stay close enough to see what he was doing.
> GARAGE FACE 100
NIA: I could. You arrived fast, turned late, and spent the whole exit correcting it.
YOU: So the car wasn't the whole problem.
NIA: No. Which is good news. We can afford to fix a habit.
JULES: Calder has five short heats before my courier run. We can use all five.

@ D07 GARAGE FACE
YOU: You put tape on the windscreen.
NIA: It's a reference mark. Watch when the corner reaches it. We aren't chasing Kade tonight.
YOU: What are we chasing?
NIA: The same corner, twice, without two different emergencies.

@ D08 MEET PAN
JULES: I followed you through practice. Your exit's quieter now.
YOU: The steering stopped feeling like an argument.
JULES: Good. Tonight, pick one line and finish it. Don't improve it halfway through.
YOU: Is that driving advice or advice about your deliveries?
JULES: Both. The second version costs extra.

@ D09 GARAGE FACE
NIA: Three heats, three decent finishes. That's a start.
YOU: Does it cover the envelope?
NIA: It covers this week. Don't make tonight carry the whole month.
YOU: Short course again?
NIA: Short course, ordinary entry, ordinary money. Boring can keep a garage open.

@ D10 MARINA RADIO
MINA: I've got our results written on the back of a takeaway menu.
YOU: Very professional.
MINA: We can afford a notebook after tonight. For now, your personal best shares a page with noodles.
NIA: Bank a clean result. Tomorrow we sleep in.
JULES: Nobody told me about sleeping in.

@ D11 MEET FACE
JULES: Calder let me choose tomorrow's courier circuit. I'm inviting you.
YOU: Another lesson?
JULES: A proper race this time. You learned to leave a corner. Let's see whether you can link a whole lap.
YOU: And if I finish ahead?
JULES: I'll stop calling it Nia's loaner. For a week.

@ D12 MEET PAN
JULES: Everyone gets the same start. No shortcuts through the loading bay. I know that trick because I invented it.
CALDER: Then you can help me put a barrier there. Get your cars to the line.
YOU: Ready when you are.
> MARINA PAN 210
NARRATOR: COURIER CIRCUIT. The last corner opens, and this time Jules has to chase your exit.
JULES: All right. That's your car tonight.
YOU: Just tonight?
JULES: Don't get greedy. I've also got a club map and a few people you should meet.
> GARAGE FACE 128
NIA: You can bring those people here. The spare chairs are doing nothing useful.
JULES: I was hoping you'd say that.

@ D13 MARINA RADIO
JULES: Take the long way to the meet. There's a club using the dock loop after sundown.
YOU: More training?
JULES: Some. Mostly they pay promptly, and Sunline needs that more than another dramatic showdown.
NIA: He's learning. Put him on the invoice.

@ D14 GARAGE FACE
MINA: There are four people outside asking whether the garage is open.
NIA: It's been open since six.
MINA: I meant for sitting around and talking about cars.
YOU: Open the shutters. We can move the chairs after tonight's heat.
NIA: Fine. Nobody puts a drink on a customer's roof.

@ D15 GARAGE FACE
YOU: A notebook. With actual paper.
MINA: Bought with our last result. Your lap times no longer smell of soy sauce.
JULES: Mine still do. I brought dinner.
NIA: Tonight's entry is paid. Eat first. Small victories count too.

@ D16 MARINA PAN
CALDER: Two dockside heats tonight. Same course, different starting order.
YOU: Why swap the order?
CALDER: So you learn to race the people around you, not the story you told yourself about where you belong.
JULES: He means don't get sulky if I start in front.
YOU: You could have led with that.

@ D17 GARAGE RADIO
NIA: I don't need one heroic lap tonight. Give me two you could repeat after a bad night's sleep.
YOU: That's oddly specific.
NIA: Jules found the kettle and told stories until two. We're all testing that theory.
JULES: Nobody asked me to stop.
MINA: The kettle did.

@ D18 GARAGE FACE
MINA: The printer's jammed. I was making a little Sunline sign for the meets.
YOU: What does it say?
MINA: 'Independent garage. Reasonable people. Unreasonable hours.'
NIA: Leave the last bit off. We need tonight's heat to pay for the ink, not encourage more visitors at midnight.

@ D19 MEET PAN
JULES: See that lamp? I used to turn in when it disappeared behind the mirror.
YOU: Used to?
JULES: Then they moved it. Nearly taught the barrier a lesson.
NIA: Find the corner, not the furniture. Tonight's course is a good place to practice that.

@ D20 MEET FACE
CALDER: People have started asking when you're racing again.
YOU: I should put that on Mina's sign.
CALDER: Put it in your head instead. They're neighbors, not a crowd you need to impress.
MINA: Too late. Mrs. Vale brought a bag of oranges with your number on it.
YOU: Now there's pressure.

@ D21 GARAGE FACE
NIA: That's the last overdue bill.
YOU: We did it?
NIA: We bought time. The owner still wants an answer about the lease, but now it can be an answer we choose.
YOU: Calder's final is still ahead.
NIA: Then tonight is another ordinary club night. Not everything needs to be the final.

@ D22 MEET PAN
CALDER: Home course tonight. Does that make it easier?
YOU: I know where the road goes.
CALDER: So does everyone else here. Familiarity isn't a free lap.
JULES: He's been saying that since I was tall enough to see over a wheel.
CALDER: And eventually you'll listen.

@ D23 GARAGE RADIO
MINA: One more little meet before Calder's final. Shall I bring the camera?
YOU: You ever leave it behind?
MINA: Once. Everyone did something interesting. Never again.
NIA: Bring it. I want a picture of a normal night before this starts feeling bigger than us.

@ D24 GARAGE FACE
CALDER: Your dad used to leave that door open after closing.
NIA: People needed somewhere to go.
CALDER: He needed them too. Don't forget that part.
YOU: What do you want from tomorrow's final?
CALDER: A driver who can bring the whole evening home. Start, finish, handshake. In that order.

@ D25 MEET PAN
CALDER: Last club final of the season. No speeches at the line. Nia's father tried one once; we left without him.
NIA: He told that story differently.
YOU: I'll save mine for the finish.
> MARINA PAN 170
NARRATOR: SALTBLOCK FINAL. The flag falls over a clean last lap. Calder is waiting at the finish with his hand out.
CALDER: The waterfront clubs asked for a recommendation. They can have mine.
JULES: Lantern Mile. Later nights, better food, worse parking.
> GARAGE FACE 120
NIA: The garage still needs an answer about the lease.
YOU: What's ours?
NIA: We're staying. Now help me put another chair by the door.

@ C01 MARINA PAN
MARISOL: Calder says you know how to finish an evening without making enemies.
YOU: Jules wasn't pleased about that last lap.
JULES: I have recovered generously.
MARISOL: Good. Lantern Mile runs on favors, food stalls, and people cleaning up after themselves. Welcome.

@ C02 MARINA FACE
MARISOL: See those harbor lights? Half the people who keep them on race with us after work.
YOU: Including you?
MARISOL: Especially me. Tonight you meet them. You can worry about beating them tomorrow.
MINA: I'm photographing the food van first. For research.

@ C03 MEET PAN
IMANI: You parked across the marshal's entrance.
YOU: I thought that was the queue.
IMANI: It was. Then everyone followed you. I'm Imani; I'll help you move them before the heat starts.
YOU: Not quite the first impression I wanted.
IMANI: I've had worse. Try not to make it your signature move.

@ C04 MARINA FACE
MINA: These people have matching awnings. We have a sign the printer chewed.
NIA: An awning won't tighten a wheel nut.
MARISOL: Neither will pride. Borrow one of ours if it rains. Bring it back dry when you can.
YOU: We can manage that.

@ C05 MARINA FACE
MARISOL: A local supplier wants to meet the newer crews. There's a place at the table if you keep showing up.
YOU: Is that a sponsorship offer?
MARISOL: It's a conversation. Don't spend it before you've had it.
NIA: Good. We're very experienced at not spending things.

@ C06 MEET PAN
JULES: Harbor loop again tonight. I know a quicker way to the start.
IMANI: Is it through the loading bay?
JULES: Not since Calder put that barrier there.
YOU: We'll take the long way. We need the practice more than the shortcut.

@ C07 MARINA RADIO
NIA: Rain on the waterfront. Give yourself room to discover how much grip you've actually got.
YOU: And if everyone else disappears into the distance?
IMANI: Let them. You can't borrow their tires by following closely enough.
MINA: You can borrow Marisol's awning, though. I've already checked.

@ C08 MARINA PAN
MINA: The supplier gave me a card. 'Come back with a few consistent results.'
YOU: So tonight buys us another line on the notebook.
MINA: Exactly. No mysterious rival, no grand announcement. Just a receipt that doesn't embarrass us.
NIA: Frame that one. It's the most realistic plan we've had.

@ C09 GARAGE FACE
YOU: I thought coming here would mean winning every conversation.
NIA: You've spent a week asking good questions. That's considerably more useful.
YOU: Even the one about wet tires?
NIA: Especially that one. Another small heat tonight. Quiet confidence suits you.

@ C10 MARINA RADIO
IMANI: You keep taking the tightest line, even when it makes the next corner awkward.
YOU: It looks shorter.
IMANI: So does sleeping on the sofa instead of going upstairs. Doesn't mean you wake up better off.
YOU: There's an upstairs?
NIA: No. She means look further ahead.

@ C11 MARINA FACE
IMANI: My shift changes tomorrow. One free evening before I disappear into work again.
YOU: You want to race?
IMANI: I want a clean hour where nobody needs anything from me. Racing seems an excellent excuse.
YOU: No favors at the line.
IMANI: That's the first sensible thing you've said to me all week.

@ C12 MARINA PAN
MARISOL: Imani picked the harbor circuit. Watch the change in surface by the warehouses.
IMANI: Don't give away all my advantages.
YOU: I noticed that patch yesterday.
IMANI: Then you've earned it. Let's go.
> MARINA PAN 215
NARRATOR: SHIFT-CHANGE DUEL. The harbor lights sweep across the finish. Imani offers a tired, satisfied smile.
IMANI: You left me room when you didn't have to. I remember things like that.

IMANI: After I sleep. That part isn't negotiable.

@ C13 MARINA FACE

@ C14 MEET PAN

@ C15 MARINA PAN

@ C16 MARINA RADIO

@ C17 MARINA FACE

@ C18 MARINA PAN

YOU: Those are becoming my favorite nights.
IMANI: Keep a few of them when this gets bigger. People forget they can enjoy something they're good at.

IMANI: If you save me a space that isn't the marshal's entrance.

@ C19 GARAGE RADIO

@ C20 MARINA FACE
MARISOL: Your name's on the harbor final list.

@ C21 MARINA PAN

@ C22 MARINA RADIO

@ C23 MARINA FACE

@ C24 GARAGE FACE

@ C25 MARINA PAN

> MARINA PAN 80

> FOUNDRY PAN 230

> GARAGE FACE 80

@ B04 FOUNDRY PAN

@ B05 GARAGE FACE

@ B06 FOUNDRY RADIO

@ B07 FOUNDRY PAN

@ B08 GARAGE FACE

MINA: He's very demanding.

@ B09 FOUNDRY FACE

ROOK: It is, if you want it to pay for a garage.

@ B10 FOUNDRY RADIO

@ B11 FOUNDRY FACE

@ B12 FOUNDRY PAN

> FOUNDRY PAN 220
NARRATOR: THE REMATCH. At the last bend, Kade leaves the smallest opening. This time your exit carries all the way to the flag.

@ B13 GARAGE FACE

@ B14 FOUNDRY FACE

@ B15 GARAGE FACE
VOSS: You've done impressive work with very little. I can pay your crew properly, secure the lease, and put you on the grid.
NIA: In exchange for Sunline's name.
VOSS: In exchange for responsibility. I have watched good garages disappear because courage couldn't meet payroll.
YOU: Did yours?
VOSS: Yes. I'd rather not see it happen to you.
NIA: Then help us build something that can stand. Don't ask us to become a sign on somebody else's wall.
VOSS: Read the offer. You owe your people that much.

@ B16 GARAGE FACE
YOU: He wasn't wrong about the wages.
NIA: No. That doesn't make the contract right. We'll put the actual choices on the table, not pretend this is easy.
MINA: First choice: tonight's club heat. It won't solve the contract, but it will pay for tomorrow.
YOU: Ordinary work, then.
NIA: Ordinary work.

@ B17 FOUNDRY PAN

@ B18 FOUNDRY RADIO

@ B19 GARAGE FACE

MINA: At his circuit. I don't have to sign away the pictures. I checked.

@ B20 FOUNDRY FACE
ROOK: My first club had a sponsor's name on the door. When the contract ended, we discovered it wasn't our door anymore.
YOU: Is that why you're helping us?
ROOK: It's why I read every page. Helping you is a separate decision.
NIA: What did we miss?
ROOK: A club can guarantee an independent team. It just needs enough members willing to stand behind it.

@ B21 FOUNDRY PAN
ROOK: Your final invitation is ready. So is a draft of the club guarantee.
YOU: We haven't won your final.
ROOK: A guarantee isn't a prize for one lap. It's a judgment about whether you'll come back when the work is dull.
NIA: We'll be back for tonight's heat too.
ROOK: That's part of my evidence.

@ B22 FOUNDRY RADIO
NIA: We're close enough to start thinking about the next chapter. That's exactly when people stop doing the things that got them here.
YOU: Same preparation. Same notes. Same last check before the grid.
NIA: Good. I was hoping I wouldn't have to give the whole speech.
JULES: I was. I'd made tea.

@ B23 FOUNDRY PAN
KADE: Last practice before Rook. She'll keep asking the same question until you give her a bad answer.

KADE: Can you do the next corner properly while somebody refuses to go away?

KADE: You're welcome.

@ B24 GARAGE FACE
NIA: Rook's members signed. So did Calder and Marisol as supporting clubs.
YOU: That's a lot of people on one piece of paper.
NIA: It should feel heavy. They didn't sign because they think we're invincible.

NIA: Win or lose. Tomorrow, remember that.

@ B25 FOUNDRY PAN
ROOK: You want a permanent circuit. Show me the patience to finish a long race first.
YOU: No miracles?
ROOK: No miracles. Just the plan you practiced.
> FOUNDRY PAN 230
NARRATOR: FOUNDRY FINAL. The last lap holds together. Rook brings two documents to the finish: the result, and the club guarantee.
ROOK: This gets you an application, not an exemption from the rules. I expect to hear how it goes.
NIA: You will. And the garage door stays open.
> PADDOCK RADIO 128
REN: Sunline? I'm Ren. Your independent application cleared its first review. Bring your notes. Meridian will give you new ones.

@ A01 PADDOCK PAN

REN: Excellent. Fewer distractions. I'll help with your first sessions.

REN: Appreciate it by bringing a pencil. I lose mine constantly.

@ A02 PADDOCK FACE

@ A03 PADDOCK RADIO

@ A04 PADDOCK PAN
MINA: A marshal stopped me taking a shortcut across the apron.

MINA: Yes. They asked you to learn the same rule before your out lap.

@ A05 PADDOCK FACE
ASTER: Your first proper grid. Do you know why the last row is important?
YOU: It gives the front row someone to underestimate?
ASTER: It gives everyone room to learn how a field moves. Take it seriously. I want you back with a result, not a grievance.
REN: That's Aster. She runs a fair circuit. Don't mistake that for an easy one.

@ A06 PADDOCK RADIO
YOU: At home I knew every sound that meant something was about to happen.
NIA: You'll learn the sounds here too. Until then, listen when Ren says wait.
REN: Wait.
YOU: That one I recognize.

@ A07 PADDOCK PAN
REN: You're turning before you've finished making space for the exit.
YOU: Kade said something like that.
REN: Sensible man. Shame about his taste in jackets.
KADE: I can hear the radio.
YOU: We have a very educational crew.

@ A08 PADDOCK RADIO
NIA: Good lap. You didn't argue with the last sector when the first one went well.
YOU: I'm trying not to celebrate while I'm still driving it.
REN: Keep that. Tonight's short session is about joining the good pieces, not collecting them separately.
MINA: I'll take the celebration photographs afterward. At a safe distance from the kettle.

@ A09 PADDOCK PAN
YOU: Another practice session instead of a big event?
NIA: Another opportunity to get paid for showing up prepared. The big event still needs fuel and somewhere to sleep.
REN: It also needs a driver who recognizes the braking boards. Practice is doing both jobs.
YOU: Ordinary work follows us everywhere.
NIA: Fortunately.

@ A10 PADDOCK FACE
MINA: First paid press pass. Look, my name's printed properly.
YOU: Put it beside the old Sunline sign.
MINA: I'm keeping both. One got me in here; the other reminds me why I wanted to come.
NIA: Just bring your own chair when the photographers visit the garage. We've run out again.

@ A11 PADDOCK FACE
REN: I submitted your sector sheets to Aster. She asked whether the driver could do it with someone beside them.
YOU: Are you volunteering?
REN: I am discovering that lending out a pencil has consequences. Event twelve. Same rules for both of us.
YOU: I'll return the pencil first.
REN: Now you're making promises you can't keep.

@ A12 PADDOCK PAN
REN: No trick setup. No secret line. Race the circuit that's in front of you, and let me worry about mine.
YOU: That might be the hardest thing you've asked all week.
> PADDOCK PAN 220
NARRATOR: SECTOR DUEL. Two cars cross the line within a breath. Ren studies the timing sheet, then finally puts the pencil down.
REN: You found the lap without borrowing it from me. That's the recommendation I wanted to write.
NIA: Stay with us for the next round?
REN: On one condition. Someone else keeps track of the pencils.
YOU: Mina has a notebook for that.

@ A13 FINALE FACE

YOU: And the name on our garage.
VOSS: The name brings obligations. I can guarantee wages, transport, a future beyond one good season.
NIA: Let us discuss it as a crew. Not just the two people you invited into this room.
VOSS: Fair. Bring me an answer, not a slogan.

@ A14 GARAGE FACE
JULES: A steady wage isn't a small thing. I've been paid late by people who were very proud of being independent.
MINA: And a contract isn't automatically a cage. Mine let me keep my photographs.
NIA: This one doesn't let us keep the garage name. That matters to me. I need to know what matters to you.
YOU: We should decide what we're building before we decide who can buy it.
REN: Put the clauses beside the actual budget. Nobody should have to choose between a speech and a meal.

@ A15 GARAGE FACE
NIA: We can meet the season's costs with the club guarantee and the work already booked. No miracle sponsorship required.
JULES: Then I can afford to say no to the parts I don't like.
MINA: And I can keep doing my own paid work without leaving the crew.
YOU: Nobody owns anyone's name here.
NIA: Including me. I needed to hear that as much as Voss does.

@ A16 PADDOCK RADIO
REN: Next block: strategy. Not a plot twist. A series of sessions where we stop improvising every decision.

REN: Good. I'd like the next problem to be something a timing sheet can help with.
NIA: You can have three practice heats and the least broken clipboard.

@ A17 PADDOCK FACE

@ A18 PADDOCK PAN
JULES: I watched the long session. Looked as if nothing happened for ages.

@ A19 PADDOCK RADIO

@ A20 PADDOCK PAN

@ A21 PADDOCK FACE

@ A22 PADDOCK RADIO

@ A24 PADDOCK FACE

> PADDOCK PAN 230

> FINALE FACE 100

> GARAGE FACE 120
